upload_params.title: These Tires Hit the Runway at 150 MPH ✈️
upload_params.description:
Jet tires slam into the runway at about 150 mph without even spinning, so they skid and smoke. Here's how they survive: about 200 psi of dry nitrogen, little plugs in the wheel that melt before a hot tire can burst, and fresh tread put on the same tire again and again.

Sources: 14 CFR 25.733 (FAA); FAA AC 20-97B and AC 145-4A; US patents 4628953 and 3138406; Simple Flying.

Subscribe to @WaitThatReallyHappenedUS for more of how big machines really work.

#shorts #aviation #airplane #engineering #howitworks #pilot

script.title: These Tires Hit the Runway at 150 MPH
sources: Simple Flying / AeroHaber, 'How Commercial Aircraft Tires Survive 150mph Runway Contact Under 20 Tonnes Of Weight Without Bursting' (touchdown around 150 mph)

SWISS magazine, 'Why do airplane tires cause smoke at touchdown?' and Physics Forums 'Commercial aircraft tire skids': wheels are not turning at touchdown, they skid briefly while spinning up, rubber smokes
The Points Guy, 'All about aircraft tires' and Simple Flying: airliner tires inflated to about 200 psi, roughly six times a car tire (car ~32-35 psi)
14 CFR 25.733(e) (Cornell LII, GovInfo): airplanes over 75,000 lb must inflate tires on braked wheels with dry nitrogen or other inert gas, max 5% oxygen
FAA AC 20-97B 'Aircraft Tire Maintenance and Operational Practices' (nitrogen inflation, heat)
Google Patents US4628953 'Fusible plug safety device for venting aircraft tires' and US3138406 'Fuse plugs for wheels': plugs in the wheel melt from brake heat and vent the tire before it can burst
Migflug, 'Aircraft Tyres and Carbon Brakes: Nitrogen, Retreads and Fuse Plugs'
FAA AC 145-4A 'Inspection, Retread, Repair, and Alterations of Aircraft Tires': worn aircraft tires are retreaded and reused

lines.text: These tires hit the runway at a hundred fifty miles an hour, without even spinning.
lines.caps: These tires hit the runway | at 150 miles an hour, | without even spinning.

lines.text: For a split second they skid, and the rubber goes up in smoke.
lines.caps: For a split second | they skid, | and the rubber goes up in smoke.

lines.text: To carry the jet, they're pumped to about two hundred psi, six times a car tire.
lines.caps: To carry the jet, | they're pumped to about 200 psi, | 6 times a car tire.

lines.text: But hard braking makes the brakes glow hot,
lines.caps: But hard braking | makes the brakes glow hot,

lines.text: so the tires are filled with dry nitrogen, which can't feed a fire the way air can.
lines.caps: so the tires are filled | with dry nitrogen, | which can't feed a fire | the way air can.

lines.text: And if the heat still climbs, little plugs in the wheel melt,
lines.caps: And if the heat still climbs, | little plugs | in the wheel melt,

lines.text: and let the gas out, so the tire goes flat instead of bursting.
lines.caps: and let the gas out, | so the tire goes flat | instead of bursting.

lines.text: When the tread wears down, they don't throw the tire away.
lines.caps: When the tread wears down, | they don't throw | the tire away.

lines.text: They put fresh tread on the same tire, again and again.
lines.caps: They put fresh tread | on the same tire, | again and again.

lines.text: That's why jet tires almost never pop, even at a hundred fifty miles an hour.
lines.caps: That's why jet tires | almost never pop, | even at 150 miles an hour.
